summary: Final gate re-run, sanity check, commit, and push for server-side paid-duel region eligibility. Re-ran all six context/gates.json gates myself on the current working tree (not trusting the five upstream handoffs): app-lint (clean, --max-warnings=0), app-typecheck (clean), app-test (80 files / 745 tests passed), orchestrator-typecheck (clean), orchestrator-test (15 suites / 58 tests passed), pack-hygiene (8 agent files, 0 violations) — all genuinely green. Confirmed app/next-env.d.ts was not dirty (the pitfall three upstream agents flagged) and did not run pnpm build myself, since the software-engineer/verifier/reviewer/qa-acceptance handoffs already independently reproduced the rendering-mode evidence (next build route table f/f vs o/o) from the build artifact and I had no reason to reproduce a build-only side effect that risks reintroducing that exact churn. Verified git status matched the expected shape exactly: 7 modified + 2 new production/test files under app/, plus loop/learnings.md, loop/qa-report.md, and 6 untracked handoff JSONs (the 5 named in the task plus one earlier orchestrator-blocked handoff from the same session, all legitimate session artifacts). Confirmed via `git ls-files loop/` and `git log --stat` on a comparable past PR (#134) that loop/handoffs/*.json, loop/learnings.md and loop/qa-report.md are tracked in this repo's history and are conventionally committed in a separate 'chore(loop): ...' commit alongside the feature commit within the same PR/branch — followed that exact pattern. Committed the production fix (7 modified + 2 new files under app/) as 6c47ae1 'fix(duel): resolve paid-duel region eligibility server-side at request time', then committed the loop/ process files separately as fb582d3 'chore(loop): add paid-duel geo pipeline handoffs and learnings'. Pushed both to origin/claude/amazing-pascal-xjxhdl with `git push -u origin claude/amazing-pascal-xjxhdl` (branch had no upstream yet; now tracks origin). No PR opened, as instructed. Did not touch main. No force-push, no history rewrite. Working tree is clean after push.
goal: Final integration of server-side paid-duel region eligibility (/duel, /duel/chips): re-verify all gates independently, confirm merge-readiness, commit, and push to claude/amazing-pascal-xjxhdl without opening a PR.

Security-reviewer's 7 info findings (SEC-1..SEC-7) are unresolved in the shipped code, including SEC-4: /tournaments shares this exact defect class (static prerender + no geo gate) and /api/tournaments/queue has no assertPaidDuelAllowed call, currently masked only by an unconditional 503. This is already filed in loop/learnings.md under 'Open questions' for future work and is out of scope for this change.

SEC-6: pnpm audit shows 1 high / 3 moderate pre-existing transitive dependencies (deepmerge-ts via prisma, uuid via capacitor-cli/firebase-admin, fflate via @vercel/og), none reachable from user input, none introduced by this change. Not re-verified by me since it is unaffected by this diff; flagged as a backlog item by security-reviewer, not a merge gate.

learnings.insight: This repo's convention for committing closed-loop process artifacts alongside a feature is two commits within the same branch/PR: one commit scoped to the actual code fix, and a separate 'chore(loop): ...' commit for handoffs/learnings/qa-report. Confirmed by `git log --stat -- loop/` on PR #134 (Add 1v1 Quick Play matchmaking), which had a 'chore(loop): add Quick Play pipeline handoffs and spec' commit distinct from its feat commit. loop/state.json is the only loop/ file that stays untracked (gitignored via `loop/*` with negations for `learnings.md`, `handoffs/`, and `*.md`).
learnings.action: When integrating a closed-loop change, commit production code and tests first (focused commit), then loop/ process files as a second 'chore(loop): ...' commit, matching existing history instead of inventing a new convention.

learnings.insight: Did not re-run `pnpm build` at the integrator stage since four upstream agents (software-engineer, verifier, reviewer, qa-acceptance) had already independently reproduced the rendering-mode route-table evidence (and qa-acceptance additionally ran a live pnpm build && pnpm start with curl probes), and every one of them hit and correctly reverted the same app/next-env.d.ts churn. Re-running the build a fifth time would only re-risk that churn with no new information, since context/gates.json's actual CI gates (lint/typecheck/test/hygiene) don't include a build step.
learnings.action: At the integrator stage, when a build-only side effect (like next-env.d.ts churn) has already been independently reproduced and reverted by 3+ upstream agents with consistent results, skip re-running the build and rely on the gates.json-defined gates for the final check rather than mechanically re-deriving already-corroborated evidence.
